body:
OBSERVED, confirmed independently (Opus).

`delete_book_from_table()` returns a structured result describing failure:
- `cps/editbooks.py:1615-1624` returns a `"type": "danger"` payload when
  `helper.delete_book` fails to remove the format file;
- `cps/editbooks.py:1596-1609` logs "removed from the database but file ..." on the
  whole-book path;
- `cps/editbooks.py:1669-1679` returns a danger payload after `session.rollback()`
  on exception.

Both SPA endpoints throw that return value away and answer unconditionally:
`cps/api/edit.py:423-426` (`delete_book`) and `cps/api/edit.py:438-442`
(`delete_format`) both end `delete_book_from_table(...)` / `return "", 204`.

So a deletion that failed, rolled back, or orphaned a file reports HTTP 204 No Content
— indistinguishable from success. React then treats it as a successful mutation and
evicts the cached rows (`frontend/src/lib/queries.ts:778-795,816-826`), so the UI shows
the book gone whether or not it is.

Classic surfaces the same conditions as a flash error. This is a strict safety
regression in the new UI relative to the old.

Fix shape: translate the core's result into a non-2xx error (and an explicit warning
response for the partial-success cases) rather than swallowing it.
title: SPA delete endpoints discard the deletion core's result and always return 204
